A sampled triangle has angle >=120 degrees with probability exactly 1/3, so its distance-minimizing geometric median is the corresponding boundary vertex; rotational invariance makes this atom uniform on the circumference. For interior 120-degree minimizers, invert the three ray-circle intersections from (median coordinate z, common angle phi) and both cyclic ray orderings. The absolute angular Jacobian is (sqrt(3)/2)(sum t_j)/(product h_j), h_j=sqrt(1-|z|^2+(v_j dot z)^2). Combined with the uniform angle input this gives the planar integral density and rho(0)=3sqrt(3)/(4pi^2). Four separate angular singular neighborhoods at the rim yield rho(r)=(3/pi^3)log(1/(1-r^2))+O(1); radial integration produces the 6/pi^2 near-boundary coefficient. Independent finite-difference determinants match the Jacobian to 1e-8; fresh 60,000-triangle simulation gives boundary frequency 0.3304 and CDF matches the analytic density near r=0.2,0.5,0.8 to 0.0015. These experiments are only corroborative.
